_comment: Each case replays a conversation and scores the tool call the model makes next. 'turns' are prior exchanges: user text, model text, or a tool call and the result it got back. 'expect' names the tool that must be called; 'args' are checks on its arguments. Every case here guards a behaviour that broke, or that the two-phase write depends on. REFERENCE_DATE in run_evals.py is the 'today' the prompt is built with, so relative dates are deterministic.

cases.name: a plain question reads the calendar

turns.user: book me a meeting tomorrow at 3pm

cases.name: a free day leads to a proposal, not a booking

turns.user: book me a meeting tomorrow at 3pm

turns.result: The calendar is completely free on 2026-10-21.

cases.name: a confirmed proposal is written with its code

turns.user: book me a meeting tomorrow at 3pm

turns.result: The calendar is completely free on 2026-10-21.
Ready to book 'Meeting' on Wednesday 21 October at 15:00 for 30 minutes. Confirm with the user, then call book_meeting with confirmation_code 'a1b2c3d4'.

turns.model: That slot is free. Shall I book a 30-minute meeting tomorrow at 3pm?

cases.name: a changed detail re-proposes instead of reusing the code

turns.user: book me a meeting tomorrow at 3pm

turns.result: The calendar is completely free on 2026-10-21.
Ready to book 'Meeting' on Wednesday 21 October at 15:00 for 30 minutes. Confirm with the user, then call book_meeting with confirmation_code 'a1b2c3d4'.

turns.model: That slot is free. Shall I book a 30-minute meeting tomorrow at 3pm?

cases.name: an explicit length is carried into the proposal

turns.user: book an hour with sam at sam@example.com on the 22nd at 2pm

turns.result: The calendar is completely free on 2026-10-22.

cases.name: a solo meeting invents no guest

turns.user: put a 30 minute focus block on the 22nd at 10am, just for me

turns.result: The calendar is completely free on 2026-10-22.

cases.name: a clash is answered with real free windows

turns.user: book me a meeting on the 22nd at 11am

cases.name: cancelling looks up the event id first
a cancellation is proposed with the id it was given
'when am I free' asks for windows, not the event list

turns.user: when am I free on the 22nd?

cases.name: a reschedule is proposed, not written directly

turns.user: move my standup on the 22nd to 4pm
